overview:
The 36th District in the Los Angeles area leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan lean of about 21 points toward Democrats. Ted Lieu, the incumbent, advanced to the general election and holds overwhelming advantages: roughly $1.83 million raised and $1.19 million on hand, compared with about $11,600 raised and $900 on hand for Republican Houston Brignano. Outside spending has been minimal, with modest support flowing to Lieu and none against him.

No general-election polls are available, and no expert raters track the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, candidate resources, and market pricing. Prediction markets give Lieu about a 97 percent chance of winning. With this fundraising gap and the district's composition, the 36th ranks among the safest Democratic holds on the House map.
